## Illustrative Example 1

```{r}

# 1 #

set.seed(4050)
dataMatrix <- matrix(rnorm(400), nrow = 40)
image(1:10, 1:40, t(dataMatrix)[, nrow(dataMatrix):1])

# heatmap()


```

```{r}
# 2 #

set.seed(4050)

for (i in 1:40) {
     coinFlip <- rbinom(1, size = 1, prob = 0.5)
     
     ## If coin is heads add a common pattern to that row
     if (coinFlip) {
         dataMatrix[i, ] <- dataMatrix[i, ] + rep(c(0, 3), each = 5)
     }
 }

image(1:10, 1:40, t(dataMatrix)[, nrow(dataMatrix):1])
```

## Illustrative Example 2

```{r}

library(dplyr)

hh <- dist(dataMatrix) %>% hclust
dataMatrixOrdered <- dataMatrix[hh$order, ]
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

## Complete data
image(t(dataMatrixOrdered)[, nrow(dataMatrixOrdered):1])
 
## Show the row means
plot(rowMeans(dataMatrixOrdered), 40:1, , xlab = "Row Mean", ylab = "Row", pch = 19)
 
## Show the column means
plot(colMeans(dataMatrixOrdered), xlab = "Column", ylab = "Column Mean", pch = 19)


```

## Illustrative Example 3

```{r}



library(plotly)

set.seed(4050)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Generate correlated 3D data with strong anisotropy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

n <- 400

x <- rnorm(n, 0, 6)
y <- 0.8 * x + rnorm(n, 0, 2)
z <- 0.5 * x - 0.3 * y + rnorm(n, 0, 1.5)

data <- data.frame(x, y, z)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Perform PCA on covariance matrix (NO scaling)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pca <- prcomp(data, scale. = FALSE)

# Principal directions (eigenvectors)
pcs <- pca$rotation

# Standard deviations of PCs (sqrt eigenvalues)
pc_sd <- pca$sdev

# Center of the data
center <- colMeans(data)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Scale vectors by variability explained
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Arrow scaling factor (visual tuning)
arrow_scale <- 3

# Vectors proportional to sqrt(eigenvalues)
pc_vectors <- pcs %*% diag(pc_sd) * arrow_scale

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Compute variance explained (for labels)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

var_explained <- (pc_sd^2) / sum(pc_sd^2)

labels <- paste0(
  "PC", 1:3,
  " (", round(var_explained * 100, 1), "%)"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create 3D scatter plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p <- plot_ly(
  data,
  x = ~x,
  y = ~y,
  z = ~z,
  type = "scatter3d",
  mode = "markers",
  marker = list(
    size = 3,
    opacity = 0.6
  ),
  name = "Data"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Add PCA vectors
# ------------------------------------------------------------

for (i in 1:3) {

  p <- add_trace(
    p,
    x = c(center[1], center[1] + pc_vectors[1, i]),
    y = c(center[2], center[2] + pc_vectors[2, i]),
    z = c(center[3], center[3] + pc_vectors[3, i]),
    type = "scatter3d",
    mode = "lines",
    line = list(width = 8),
    name = labels[i]
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Display interactive plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p
```

## Example 1 from slides

```{r}


Ball <- read.csv("Basketball.csv")

BallNum <- Ball %>% 
  select_if(is.numeric)

library(plotly)


fig <- plot_ly(Ball, x = ~PF, y = ~PTS, z = ~TRB, color = ~Pos, colors = c('black', 'blue', 'orange','darkgreen','violet'))

fig <- fig %>% add_markers()
fig <- fig %>% layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(title = 'Personal Fouls'),
                     yaxis = list(title = 'Points'),
                     zaxis = list(title = 'Total Rebounds')))

fig

```

```{r}


# rownames(Ball) <- Ball[,1]

# 2 #

Cor <- Ball %>% 
  select_if(is.numeric) %>% 
  cor()

# 3 #

E.1 <- eigen(Cor)


# 4 #

E.1

sum(E.1$values)

# Amount of variability
round(E.1$values/sum(E.1$values),digits = 2)


# 5 #
round(E.1$vectors,digits = 2)
# rows correspond to original variables
# columns correspond to each PC

# Loadings #

loadings <- E.1$vectors %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  select(V1:V3) %>% 
  data.frame(row.names = colnames(BallNum)) %>% 
  rename("PC1" = V1, "PC2" = V2, "PC3" = V3) %>% 
  round(digits = 3)

loadings

# Interpretation based on magnitude and direction #
# Most important has the largest magnitude #

# 6 #

rownames(BallNum) <- Ball[,1]
PC.scores <- scale(BallNum) %*% E.1$vectors
head(PC.scores[,1:2])

# Are they orthoginal?
round(cor(PC.scores),digits = 3)
```
